'''Horus Procession''' is an ancient Egyptian festival

==Overview==
{{Infobox hieroglyphs two-columns
|NAME = <hiero>T18-S29-G43-D54:Z2-G5</hiero><br/>Schemsu-{{ill|Horus|en|Horus|qid=Q84122|lt=Hor|1=Horus}}<br/>''Šmsw-Ḥr.w''<br/>''Servant of Horus / Horus Retinue / Horus Following''

|NAME2-ERWEITERT = {{ill|Military colours, standards and guidons|en|Military colours, standards and guidons|qid=Q2912707|lt=Fourfold Standard|1=Military colours, standards and guidons}} of the king&nbsp;<ref>The original hieroglyph of the standard of Chons (Imiut fetish) cannot currently be displayed in Wgoodbye $1’s font set.</ref>
|NAME2 = <hiero>E18-G7-G26-R12-Aa1:N35:M23-G43</hiero> <br/> {{ill|Wepwawet|en|Wepwawet|qid=Q372560|lt=Upuaut|1=Wepwawet}}, {{ill|Horus|en|Horus|qid=Q84122|lt=Horus|1=Horus}}, {{ill|Thoth (disambiguation)|en|Thoth (disambiguation)|qid=Q234267|lt=Thoth|1=Thoth (disambiguation)}} and {{ill|Khonsu|en|Khonsu|qid=Q190521|lt=Chons|1=Khonsu}}

The '''Horus retinue''' (also '''Servants of Horus, Festival of the Journey Through the Land''') {{ill|symbol|de|symbol|ja|symbol|zh|symbol|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/symbol|1=Symbol (typeface)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q187829}} initially symbolized the {{ill|Pharaoh|de|Pharaoh|ja|Pharaoh|zh|Pharaoh|lt=King|lt_ja=King|lt_de=King|lt_zh=King|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pharaoh|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} as a living {{ill|Horus|en|Horus|qid=Q84122|lt=Horus|1=Horus}}, in whose train other deities of {{ill|Ancient Egypt|en|Ancient Egypt|qid=Q11768|lt=Ancient Egypt|1=Ancient Egypt}} stood, and is attested in {{ill|Egyptian Mythology|de|Egyptian Mythology|ja|Egyptian Mythology|zh|Egyptian Mythology|lt=Ancient Egyptian mythology|lt_ja=Ancient Egyptian mythology|lt_de=Ancient Egyptian mythology|lt_zh=Ancient Egyptian mythology|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Egyptian Mythology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} as early as the {{ill|Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)|de|Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)|ja|Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)|zh|Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)|lt=Thinite Period|lt_ja=Thinite Period|lt_de=Thinite Period|lt_zh=Thinite Period|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. At that time, Horus was regarded as the all-encompassing sky god and shows connections to the goddess {{ill|Mafdet|en|Mafdet|qid=Q845626|lt=Mafdet|1=Mafdet}}, who, as the bearer of the {{ill|Leopard skin (clothing in Ancient Egypt)|en|Leopard skin (clothing in Ancient Egypt)|qid=Q1486568|lt=Sky Leopard Skin|1=Leopard skin (clothing in Ancient Egypt)}}, possessed characteristics later attributed to {{ill|Osiris|en|Osiris|qid=Q46491|lt=Osiris|1=Osiris}}.

Mit the introduction in the {{ill|3rd Dynasty|de|3rd Dynasty|ja|3rd Dynasty|zh|3rd Dynasty|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/3rd Dynasty|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the worship of the {{ill|Sun God|de|Sun God|ja|Sun God|zh|Sun God|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sun God|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} {{ill|Re (Egyptian mythology)|de|Re (Egyptian mythology)|ja|Re (Egyptian mythology)|zh|Re (Egyptian mythology)|lt=Re|lt_ja=Re|lt_de=Re|lt_zh=Re|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Re (Egyptian mythology)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a change in significance ensued, as the king now represented the personified sun deity as the firstborn son of Re. With the later establishment of {{ill|Court (disambiguation)|en|Court (disambiguation)|qid=Q293634|lt=Court|1=Court (disambiguation)}} halls in {{ill|Memphis (Egypt)|de|Memphis (Egypt)|ja|Memphis (Egypt)|zh|Memphis (Egypt)|lt=Memphis|lt_ja=Memphis|lt_de=Memphis|lt_zh=Memphis|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Memphis (Egypt)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the processions of the Horus retinue came to an end – along with the associated {{ill|Cattle count|de|Cattle Count in Ancient Egypt|ja|Cattle Count in Ancient Egypt|zh|Cattle Count in Ancient Egypt|lt=Cattle Count|lt_ja=Cattle Count|lt_de=Cattle Count|lt_zh=Cattle Count|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cattle count|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Judiciary|de|Judiciary|ja|Judiciary|zh|Judiciary|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Judiciary|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.

== Royal Cult ==
In the depictions on the {{ill|Turin Royal Papyrus|de|Turin Royal Papyrus|ja|Turin Royal Papyrus|zh|Turin Royal Papyrus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Turin Royal Papyrus|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the early kings are also listed, explicitly designated with respect to their {{ill|Horus name|de|Horus Names|ja|Horus Names|zh|Horus Names|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horus name|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} as “Servants of Horus” or “Successors of Horus”. The calendrical entries on the {{ill|Palermo Stone|de|Palermo Stone|ja|Palermo Stone|zh|Palermo Stone|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Palermo Stone|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} title the cattle count, in the context of tax levies, as the solemn {{ill|Procession|de|Procession|ja|Procession|zh|Procession|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Procession|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the “Horus retinue”.

=== Fourfold Standard ===
On the {{ill|Narmer Palette|de|Narmer Palette|ja|Narmer Palette|zh|Narmer Palette|lt=Narmer Palette|lt_ja=Narmer Palette|lt_de=Narmer Palette|lt_zh=Narmer Palette|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Narmer Palette|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the king, during a procession, wears the {{ill|Lower Egypt|de|Lower Egypt|ja|Lower Egypt|zh|Lower Egypt|lt=red crown of Lower Egypt|lt_ja=red crown of Lower Egypt|lt_de=red crown of Lower Egypt|lt_zh=red crown of Lower Egypt|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lower Egypt|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, followed by a sandal-bearer whose title is marked with the {{ill|Ideogram|de|Ideogram|ja|Ideogram|zh|Ideogram|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ideogram|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the goddess {{ill|Seshat|en|Seshat|qid=Q478490|lt=Seschat|1=Seshat}}. Preceding the king is a panther-pelt bearer designated as {{ill|Tjet|de|Tjet|ja|Tjet|zh|Tjet|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tjet|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and ahead of him, four smaller figures serve as the king’s standard bearers at the head of the procession. These four standards represent the classic fourfold standard, which customarily symbolizes the divine attributes of the king.

The {{ill|Falcon (disambiguation)|en|Falcon (disambiguation)|qid=Q223837|lt=Falcon|1=Falcon (disambiguation)}} portrays the king as the divine ruler, while the {{ill|Ibis (disambiguation)|en|Ibis (disambiguation)|qid=Q294079|lt=Ibis|1=Ibis (disambiguation)}} appears as the manifestation of the nocturnal {{ill|Moon Deity|de|Moon Deity|ja|Moon Deity|zh|Moon Deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moon Deity|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Thoth. Falcon and Ibis thus appeared as representatives of the two times of day – {{ill|Day (disambiguation)|en|Day (disambiguation)|qid=Q246899|lt=Day|1=Day (disambiguation)}} representing “activity”, “conquest”, “expansion” and the “sky god”, and {{ill|Night (disambiguation)|en|Night (disambiguation)|qid=Q69327093|lt=Night|1=Night (disambiguation)}} representing “procreation”, “magic”, the {{ill|Duat|en|Duat|qid=Q871389|lt=Land of Light of the Afterlife|1=Duat}} and the “{{ill|Centripetal Force|de|Centripetal Force|ja|Centripetal Force|zh|Centripetal Force|lt=Completer of the Cycle|lt_ja=Completer of the Cycle|lt_de=Completer of the Cycle|lt_zh=Completer of the Cycle|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Centripetal Force|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}”.

The {{ill|Jackal (disambiguation)|en|Jackal (disambiguation)|qid=Q3157371|lt=Jackal|1=Jackal (disambiguation)}} or {{ill|Wolf|en|Wolf|qid=Q18498|lt=Wolf|1=Wolf}} served as the symbol for the deity Upuaut, who identified the king as the firstborn and, in a dual function, as the accompanying “Opener of the Ways” – both as the “Opener of the Ways” to the afterlife for the deceased and as the “Opener of the Ways” for the newborn in the birth canal. Finally, the {{ill|Chons Symbol|de|Chons Symbol|ja|Chons Symbol|zh|Chons Symbol|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chons Symbol|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} united the cycle of death and {{ill|Reincarnation|en|Reincarnation|qid=Q128593|lt=Reincarnation|1=Reincarnation}}. In {{ill|Egyptology|de|Egyptology|ja|Egyptology|zh|Egyptology|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Egyptology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the fourfold standard is generally designated as the “Horus retinue”, although on other occasions the “open standard” also functioned as the “Horus retinue”.

=== Open Standard ===
The open standard appeared in iconographic representations whenever the king, as the “living Horus”, carried out the functions of “conqueror of enemies”, “lord of the world” and “conqueror”. The term “open standard” derives from the interchangeability of the depicted deities and was used in various ceremonies.

{{ill|Seth (Egyptian mythology)|de|Seth (Egyptian mythology)|ja|Seth (Egyptian mythology)|zh|Seth (Egyptian mythology)|lt=Seth|lt_ja=Seth|lt_de=Seth|lt_zh=Seth|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seth (Egyptian mythology)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} could, prior to his interim {{ill|Vehmic court|en|Vehmic court|qid=Q639898|lt=defamation|1=Vehmic court}}, be taken into account in military conflicts just as {{ill|Min|en|Min|qid=Q224634|lt=Min|1=Min}} was in connection with the {{ill|King's Festival Calendar|de|Festkalender des Königs|ja|King's Festival Calendar|zh|King's Festival Calendar|lt=King's Renewal Festivals|lt_ja=King's Renewal Festivals|lt_de=King's Renewal Festivals|lt_zh=King's Renewal Festivals|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/King's Festival Calendar|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, for example, the {{ill|Min Festival|de|Min Festival|ja|Min Festival|zh|Min Festival|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Min Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Sed Festival|de|Sed Festival|ja|Sed Festival|zh|Sed Festival|lt=Sed Festival|lt_ja=Sed Festival|lt_de=Sed Festival|lt_zh=Sed Festival|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sed Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Also belonging to the open standard and thus to the “Horus retinue” were female deities such as {{ill|Hathor|en|Hathor|qid=Q133343|lt=Hathor|1=Hathor}}, {{ill|Isis|en|Isis|qid=Q79876|lt=Isis|1=Isis}}, Mafdet and {{ill|Sekhmet|de|Sekhmet|ja|Sekhmet|zh|Sekhmet|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekhmet|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. In later Egyptian mythology, {{ill|Taweret|en|Taweret|qid=Q207435|lt=Taweret|1=Taweret}} is considered the “consort of Seth”, who was only admitted to the “Horus retinue” after her estrangement from Seth.

== Festival Cult ==
=== The Festival “Journey Through the Land” ===
{{Infobox hieroglyphs two-columns
|TITEL = Königsbarke
|NAME = <hiero>D58-M17-G6-P3</hiero><br/>Bak-wia<br/>''Bjk-wj3''<br/>''{{ill|Horus|en|Horus|qid=Q84122|lt=Falcon Barque (Royal Barque)|1=Horus}}''
|NAME-ERWEITERT = {{ill|Altes Reich (Ägypten)|de|Altes Reich (Ägypten)|ja|Altes Reich (Ägypten)|zh|Altes Reich (Ägypten)|lt=Old Kingdom (Egypt)|lt_ja=Old Kingdom (Egypt)|lt_de=Old Kingdom (Egypt)|lt_zh=Old Kingdom (Egypt)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Altes Reich (Ägypten)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
|BILD1 = Maquette-barque-khéops.jpg
|BILD1-BREITE = 300px
|BILD1-BESCHREIBUNG = Cheops’ barque as a Falcon Barque
}}

Originally, the king journeyed through the land every two years to administer justice and distribute gifts for outstanding achievements by the people. These activities were accompanied by the festival “Journey Through the Land”. In early times, village leaders and minor princes were responsible for the king’s provision. The standards marched alongside the king in the company of military detachments. In this context, the military unit was also regarded as the Horus retinue. The associated royal motif of “punishment of the wicked and reward for the loyal” persisted in various adaptations until the {{ill|Late Period (Egypt)|de|Late Period (Egypt)|ja|Late Period (Egypt)|zh|Late Period (Egypt)|lt=Late Period|lt_ja=Late Period|lt_de=Late Period|lt_zh=Late Period|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Period (Egypt)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.

In tomb paintings connected with the ceremonies, a ship was consistently depicted. This form of representation is attested in archaeological finds from the Negade-II period during the Naqada Culture (ca. 3500 to 3200 BC) throughout Egypt. Initially, the ship primarily served as a “container for gifts and offerings”. For this purpose, the royal ship – “Horus, the royal falcon” – symbolized the king himself as a divine emblem. The gift vessels likely contained ointments and {{ill|Anointing Oil|de|Anointing Oil|ja|Anointing Oil|zh|Anointing Oil|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anointing Oil|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, which the loyal of the land received as divine gifts. Even in later times, ointments and oils continued to hold great significance as sacred offerings. Sacrificial gifts from the populace could, in turn, be stored in the ship as it emptied.

The king sailed on the ship—on which the Horus retinue was represented in the form of divine statues housed in small {{ill|Shrine|de|Shrine|ja|Shrine|zh|Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}s—making several stops along the banks of the {{ill|Nile (disambiguation)|en|Nile (disambiguation)|qid=Q45225|lt=Nile|1=Nile (disambiguation)}}.<ref>{{ill|Björn Landström|en|Björn Landström|qid=Q436856|lt=Björn Landström|1=Björn Landström}}: ''Ships of the Pharaohs. 4000 years of Egyptian shipbuilding.'' Allen & Unwin, London 1970, p. 120.</ref> While the people celebrated on the banks of the Nile, the king acted as the divine judge of his office. As a symbol of his jurisdiction, a boundary post was erected on the forward part of the ship with the installed execution device “Schemsi”, which the king replaced—after the introduction of the Re cult—with the “post of the world-ruler Re”. For example, the forty‐meter-long royal ship of {{ill|Khufu|en|Khufu|qid=Q161904|lt=Cheops|1=Khufu}} had a cladding of {{ill|Gold|en|Gold|qid=Q897|lt=Gold|1=Gold}} and served as the “{{ill|Judiciary|de|Judiciary|ja|Judiciary|zh|Judiciary|lt=great house of justice|lt_ja=great house of justice|lt_de=great house of justice|lt_zh=great house of justice|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Judiciary|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}”.

=== From the Horus Retinue to Tax Collection ===
Initially, only the counts of gold and {{ill|Agriculture|de|Agriculture|ja|Agriculture|zh|Agriculture|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agriculture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} produce were in focus; later, the cattle count was added. These activities, following the arrival of the {{ill|Nile Flood|de|Nile Flood|ja|Nile Flood|zh|Nile Flood|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nile Flood|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, were linked to the tasks of the royal judiciary. In this framework, the king’s officials delivered the tributes of the populace. The amount of the tribute was determined by the respective livestock and the arable land to be cultivated.

The Horus retinue is attested on the {{ill|Palermo Stone|de|Palermo Stone|ja|Palermo Stone|zh|Palermo Stone|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Palermo Stone|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} since the {{ill|1st Dynasty|de|1st Dynasty|ja|1st Dynasty|zh|1st Dynasty|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1st Dynasty|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. In the second half of the 1st Dynasty, mentions of the Horus retinue initially ceased. Possibly, due to particular events, the Horus retinue temporarily receded into the background or was no longer explicitly mentioned. The exact reasons have not yet been reconstructed. However, with the beginning of the {{ill|2nd Dynasty|de|2nd Dynasty|ja|2nd Dynasty|zh|2nd Dynasty|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2nd Dynasty|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, documented processions of the Horus retinue reappear, now supplemented with the addendum “x-th cattle count (Tenut)”. From this developed a tribute that was to be paid independently of the king’s presence.

== The Horus Retinue in Funerary Cult ==
[[File:Horusgeleit1.PNG|thumb|Horus retinue as tomb painting]]
After the king’s death, his body is escorted in a funeral procession to his tomb by the Horus retinue. The standard of Upuaut or {{ill|Iunmutef|1=Iunmutef|2=de|3=Iunmutef|4=es|5=Iunmutef|6=fr|7=Iounmoutef|8=fi|9=Inmutef|de|Iunmutef|1=Iunmutef|2=de|3=Iunmutef|4=es|5=Iunmutef|6=fr|7=Iounmoutef|8=fi|9=Inmutef|ja|Iunmutef|1=Iunmutef|2=de|3=Iunmutef|4=es|5=Iunmutef|6=fr|7=Iounmoutef|8=fi|9=Inmutef|zh|Iunmutef|1=Iunmutef|2=de|3=Iunmutef|4=es|5=Iunmutef|6=fr|7=Iounmoutef|8=fi|9=Inmutef|es|Iunmutef|1=Iunmutef|2=de|3=Iunmutef|4=es|5=Iunmutef|6=fr|7=Iounmoutef|8=fi|9=Inmutef|fr|Iounmoutef|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iunmutef|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was positioned at the head of the retinue. Upuaut is, like Anubis later, a {{ill|Totengott|de|Totengott|ja|Totengott|zh|Totengott|lt=Death God|lt_ja=Death God|lt_de=Death God|lt_zh=Death God|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Totengott|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, who, as “Opener of the Ways”, accompanied the {{ill|Ba (Egyptian mythology)|de|Ba (Egyptian mythology)|ja|Ba (Egyptian mythology)|zh|Ba (Egyptian mythology)|lt=Ba souls|lt_ja=Ba souls|lt_de=Ba souls|lt_zh=Ba souls|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ba (Egyptian mythology)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} on their journey to the {{ill|Ta-djeser|de|Ta-djeser|ja|Ta-djeser|zh|Ta-djeser|lt=holy land|lt_ja=holy land|lt_de=holy land|lt_zh=holy land|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ta-djeser|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Therefore, Upuaut and Anubis bore the epithet “Lord of the Holy Land”.

In the later {{ill|Re (Egyptian mythology)|de|Re (Egyptian mythology)|ja|Re (Egyptian mythology)|zh|Re (Egyptian mythology)|lt=Re cult|lt_ja=Re cult|lt_de=Re cult|lt_zh=Re cult|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Re (Egyptian mythology)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the reciting priests performed during the {{ill|Opening of the mouth ceremony|en|Opening of the mouth ceremony|qid=Q1191513|lt=Opening of the mouth ceremony|1=Opening of the mouth ceremony}} and in preparation for the “final procession of the justified” as the king of the living: “You set out and behold Re above the heavenly post, above the bearers of the sky, above the head of Iunmutef, above the shoulder of Upuaut.” In one tomb inscription, for example, the separation of the {{ill|Ka (Egyptian mythology)|de|Ka (Egyptian mythology)|ja|Ka (Egyptian mythology)|zh|Ka (Egyptian mythology)|lt=Ka|lt_ja=Ka|lt_de=Ka|lt_zh=Ka|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ka (Egyptian mythology)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from the {{ill|Ba (Egyptian mythology)|de|Ba (Egyptian mythology)|ja|Ba (Egyptian mythology)|zh|Ba (Egyptian mythology)|lt=Ba|lt_ja=Ba|lt_de=Ba|lt_zh=Ba|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ba (Egyptian mythology)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} is described: “May you free yourself from the Ka {{ill|sefech|de|Lösung (Altes Ägypten)|ja|Solution (Ancient Egypt)|zh|Solution (Ancient Egypt)|lt=free|lt_ja=free|lt_de=free|lt_zh=free|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sefech|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, in the place where he (Re) dwells in the midst of the first Djadjat; may you become friendly with the Horus retinue.” In these ceremonies, Iunmutef, Anubis or Upuaut alternated as the “first of the Horus retinue”.

At the same time, the “direction of the procession of the Horus retinue” makes it clear that the entrance gates of the {{ill|Duat|en|Duat|qid=Q871389|lt=afterlife|1=Duat}} were not located underground but in the celestial regions in the area of {{ill|Mesqet|de|Mesqet|ja|Mesqet|zh|Mesqet|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mesqet|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
